Stampede at a synchronized expiry A cache stampede occurs when many concurrent readers miss or decide that a cached value needs refreshing, then issue many redundant expensive origin loads. **Illustrative fiction:** one key receives 600 reads/s. Without per-key coalescing or a source admission budget, the origin may receive hundreds of near-identical queries even though normally it receives few.
